questions.subject: chemistry
questions.content: Ammonia forms the complex ion [Cu(NH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>4</sub>]<sup>2+</sup> with copper ions in alkaline solutions but not in acidic solutions. What is the reason for it?

options.content:
In acidic solutions protons coordinate with ammonia molecules forming <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="SVG" overflow="overflow"><svg style="vertical-align: -0.69ex;" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="5.57ex" height="2.554ex" role="img" focusable="false" viewBox="0 -823.8 2462 1128.9" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><g stroke="currentColor" fill="currentColor" stroke-width="0" transform="scale(1,-1)"><g data-mml-node="math"><g data-mml-node="mi"><use data-c="1D441" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-I-1D441"></use></g><g data-mml-node="msubsup" transform="translate(888,0)"><g data-mml-node="mi"><use data-c="1D43B" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-I-1D43B"></use></g><g data-mml-node="mo" transform="translate(973.9,411.6) scale(0.707)"><use data-c="2B" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-N-2B"></use></g><g data-mml-node="mn" transform="translate(864,-305.1) scale(0.707)"><use data-c="34" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-N-34"></use></g></g></g></g></svg></mjx-container> ions and NH<sub>3</sub>
 molecules are not available

In alkaline solutions insoluble Cu(OH)<sub>2</sub>
 is precipitated which is soluble in excess of any alkali
Copper hydroxide is an amphoteric substance
In acidic solutions hydration protects copper ions.
